answer: The KX-100 cannot do this measurement. Its calibrated frequency range is 10 MHz to 18 GHz, so a 40 GHz signal is outside the band: SENS:FREQ 40 GHZ is refused with error -222 and any reading would carry the wrong calibration factor, with no calibrated result possible. Independently, the instrument's measurement resolution is 0.01 dB (FETC? returns two decimals) and the manual states that no setting or averaging count extends this, so 0.001 dB drift logging is not available either. You will need a power sensor rated to at least 40 GHz with 0.001 dB display resolution; the KX-100 on the bench is not suitable for this qualification.
